I'll kick things off by telling all of you about a strange place on a hiking trail I have visited several times. The trail itself is a roughly 20 mile loop tucked into the foothills of the appalachian mountains in northern Alabama. It is typically hiked as an overnight trip, as half of the hike is fairly strenuous and tough going while you scramble up boulders, gaining nearly a mile in elevation as you make your way to the top of a mountain from the forest floor. The climb is always well worth it, though.

Aside from the vistas, the trail has other interesting features. There are two fairly large1 waterfalls2 both of which have great swimming holes, an abundance of flora and fauna, and suprising few other visitors to have to share it all with. Another surprising sight, due to its over the top cliche nature, are the remains of a couple of old and long abandoned moonshining operations scattered between the hills. You can really get a sense of what the Southeastern American wilderness has to offer out here.

All of these things make the trail a wonderful place to visit, but what makes it truly strange is a campsite along a creekbed halfway into the trail. As I mentioned earlier, I have hiked this same trail several times. In all but one of those hikes, I decided to make camp in the same spot next to this creek bed. For whatever reason, and most probably it is the large boulder seen in the picture of the creek, the sounds of the water trickling down stream play tricks on your mind. When you focus on the sounds of the water flowing by, nothing appears unusual, but when you are doing something else, setting up your tent, gathering firewood, cooking dinner, etc, the sound takes on a strange character. Like muffled voices of other hikers off in the distance. You can't make out any words, it certainly isn't english or any other language for that matter, but it somehow strikes a connection in your mind that says it is distinctly human, and you could make out what was being said if only it was closer. At first you shrug it off, but after a few hours of your mind playing tricks on you it becomes almost irritating, and that is when you first notice it. You've been clenching your teeth the entire time you have been down here. Why? This is something anyone who has ever experimented with adderall or any other stimulant drugs would be familiar with, it is called bruxism, but despite what my username may suggest I was never under the influence of any substance on any of these hikes (up to this point atleast, alcohol was hared later on).You desperately want to ask your friends if they too hear what sounds like voices off in the distance, but when you are about to vocalize it, you realize how incredibly schizophrenic it would sound, so you keep it to yourself, hoping it will go away. After eating dinner, shooting the shit around the fire for a couple of hours and sharing a bit of whiskey, it is still there, but you don't care as much, and you are able to retire to your tent and sleep soundly.

The next morning, however, it is back. You still hear voices and you still grind your teeth. So intensely in fact, that you can't hardly eat your oatmeal breakfast from your teeth being so sore. You have a lot of hiking left in front of you though, so you pack up your gear and continue down the trail, and the voices and teeth grinding stay right where you left them, and they are right there waiting on you each time you return.
Have you ever had anything inexplicable happen to you? Tell us your strange stories that defy reason.
